display_name: Caesarius, brother of Gregory the Theologian

names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Καισάριος αδελφός Γρηγορίου Θεολόγου», with the rank word and the kinship clause left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 9 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети Кесарије.“, with Свети left off, which is not a rank. The heading gives no epithet and no kinship; the brother is named in the body's first clause, and the corpus puts such clauses in the English name and not in the stored form. `Кесарије` is held by no other folder.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Καισάριος αδελφός Γρηγορίου Θεολόγου»

attestations.note: The page heads him «(330 - 368)» and dates his death to 9 March 368, the day the calendar keeps him on. It names his father, his mother and his sister and gives each of them another day — the Theologian on 25 Ιανουαρίου, his father on 1 Ιανουαρίου, Nonna on 5 Αυγούστου, Gorgonia on 23 Φεβρουαρίου — and prints no hymn for Caesarius.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.03.2026 (9. март ст. ст.) — „Свети Кесарије.“

attestations.note: The day's third and last entry. The heading gives the bare forename alone and the body's first clause is what identifies him — brother of Gregory the Theologian — which is the kinship this folder's English name already carries. That clause also prints the year 369, where the folder holds saint.gr's 368 for his repose; one year apart, and the sourced year was not written over. The entry is otherwise about his theology and not his life.

birth.note: saint.gr: «γεννήθηκε στη Ναζιανζό της Καππαδοκίας το έτος 330 μ.Χ.», and the page heads him «(330 - 368)».

death.note: saint.gr: «Αρρώστησε βαριά και στις 9 Μαρτίου 368 μ.Χ. πέθανε» — he fell gravely ill and died on 9 March 368.
